title: Axis
description: One word set very large in Geist's variable font, black on warm white and running off the edges. The letter under the pointer takes its weight from where the pointer sits, hairline at the left and black at the right, and the letters either side fall away to hairline, so the word reads as a weight ramp. Moving across sends that ramp through the word like a wave, each letter a beat behind its neighbour nearer the pointer. Press and drag to lean the letters from upright to oblique; let go and they spring back. Every letter's advance is re-measured at its own weight each frame, so the spacing is set correctly at every point of the sweep.
intent: After Grilli Type's GT Haptik minisite (https://www.itsnicethat.com/articles/grilli-type-1): a specimen that teaches the weight axis with one gesture. Pointer x is the weight axis; a drag shears the glyphs about their x-height centre into a sane oblique; spacing follows the house tracking law on real per-weight advances and kerning.
